It prints the system's time in combined ISO 8601 date-and-time form with the offset, for example 2020-06-29T22:29:37+00:00, based on the system configured timezone. If you want the surrounding detail instead, 'show clock' returns current-time, universal-time, timezone, uptime, uptime-seconds, time-source, DST-active and last-time-jump.

The 'uptime' command displays the system uptime and load average, for example: '21:24:09 up 41 days, 15:56, 1 user, load average: 0.10, 0.35, 0.39'. The load average, also called average system load, indicates whether there are multiple tasks queued on the system (on the card). Whether it is high or low depends on the number of cores the system has, how many CPUs are integrated into the card, and the load average number itself. The stated rule of thumb: a load average value is considered high when it is greater than the number of CPUs on the card. The command takes no parameters and runs in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Yes. The command is 'manual-switchover [-f] [resource=]<value>' in Operational mode, where resource is the AID of the object to be switched, for example 'manual-switchover card-1-3' on a 1830 GX G42, 'manual-switchover card-1-5' on a G32, or 'manual-switchover card-1-12' on a G34c. It prompts: 'Controller will switchover and connection to the management interface will be lost. Do you want to continue? [y/n]'. You confirm at that prompt to proceed, or pass -f to force it without confirmation. So expect to lose the management connection and reconnect to the newly active controller. For the full procedure see the 1830 GX Software Management Procedures Guide.

'show protection' displays the node's protection container. It is a show-only command with no parameters, available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. For detail below it, use 'show protection-group-<name>' for group state (pg-state, pg-request, switching-mode, reversion-mode, hold-off-timer, wtr-timer, remaining-wtr, last-switch-trigger, working-pu, protection-pu) and 'show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name>' for the per-member state and role.

On protection-group, switching-mode takes unidirectional or bidirectional and defaults to unidirectional. wtr-timer is the trigger clearance soaking time before reverting to the working protection unit, measured and set in 1-second steps, with a range of 60..720 seconds and a default of 300; it is only applicable in revertive mode, and reversion-mode itself defaults to non-revertive (values revertive, non-revertive), so you must set reversion-mode revertive for the WTR timer to matter. The read-only remaining-wtr shows the time left, range 0..720 seconds, again only in revertive mode. The related hold-off-timer is the switching trigger soaking time before switching, in 1-millisecond steps, range 0..10000 ms, default 0. All are set with 'add/set protection-group-<name> ...'.

Use the operating command 'protection-switch [-f] [operation-type=]<value> [switch-target=]<value> [protection-group=]<value>' in Operational mode. operation-type takes force, lockout, manual or release; switch-target is the target of the switch and is not needed for the release and lockout operations. For example: 'protection-switch protection-group-test operation-type=force switch-target=protection'. Pass -f to skip confirmation. Equivalently the group's pg-request attribute can be set with 'set protection-group-<name> pg-request forced-to-protection'; pg-request accepts clear (default), manual-to-working, manual-to-protection, forced-to-working, forced-to-protection, protection-lockout and exercise (applicable only for bidirectional SNCP). The resulting condition appears in pg-state as forced-to-protection.

Read the state attribute of the protection units: 'show protection-unit-<protection-group-name>/<protection-unit-name> [AID] [transport-entity] [state] [role] [alarm-report-control] [label]'. state takes active, standby, available or unknown, so the member reporting active is the one carrying traffic. role tells you which member is which, taking working or protection. transport-entity gives the instance identifier of the underlying transport entity. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. At group level, 'show protection-group-<name> pg-state last-switch-trigger' tells you why the current selection is in place. Only alarm-report-control (allowed/inhibited, default inhibited) and label are settable on a protection-unit.

Most alarms have both an automatic raise criteria and a clear criteria, but a small subset have no clear criteria and require the user to acknowledge and clear them manually. Clear one with 'clear [-f] alarm [alarm-type=]<value> [[resource=]<value>[,<value>]*]', for example 'clear alarm DBRESTOREFAIL'; -f forces the command without confirmation. To find which of your stuck alarms are eligible, list the inventory entries flagged can-be-cleared-by-user: 'show alarm-inventory can-be-cleared-by-user=true'. Note the restriction: this mechanism applies only to system alarms that are not associated with any particular resource but with the system itself, that is system wide/global alarms. Access is Operational mode.

That is decided by the system wide alarm-reporting-control behavior switch, 'set alarm-control arc-behavior <value>'. It takes leave-alarms, which leaves current alarms in a raised mode when ARC is set to inhibit, or clear-alarms, which clears current alarms when ARC is set to inhibit. The default is leave-alarms, so by default alarms already raised stay up when you inhibit reporting. Change it with 'set alarm-control arc-behavior clear-alarms' and check it with 'show alarm-control'. The same object carries alarm-soaking-behavior (automatic, using the soaking time defined in the FM profile, or no-soak, where certain alarms specified in the FM profile have no soaking time; default automatic). Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. Per-object inhibiting is done with the alarm-report-control attribute (allowed/inhibited) on the entity.

Look it up in the alarm inventory, which holds all possible alarm types for the system with static information for each: 'show alarm-inventory-<alarm-type> [resource-type] [alarm-category] [alarm-type-description] [corrective-action] [default-severity] [service-affecting]', for example 'show alarm-inventory-TIM' or 'show alarm-inventory-MSIM'. alarm-type-description is the description of the alarm type (string 0..128), and corrective-action is system provided information on how to correct the situation that triggered the alarm (string 0..256). alarm-category is one of communication, facility, equipment, environmental, processing-error, software, quality-of-service or security. default-severity lists the possible defaults (critical, major, minor, warning, not-reported, event), which can differ per resource-type. service-affecting is indeterminate, sa, nsa or sa-nsa.

Yes, that is exactly what alarm-severity-entry is for: it configures the severity for one particular alarm. Use 'set alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> severity <value>', for example 'set alarm-severity-entry-OTU2/TIM/ingress/near-end severity minor' or 'set alarm-severity-entry-tom/EQPTCOMFAIL severity major'. resource-type is the card or entity type (for example CHM1R, FAN, 1830 GX G31), alarm-type is the abbreviated code (for example ADMIN-LOCK, BERSD), direction is na, ingress or egress, and location is na, near-end or far-end. severity takes critical, event, major, minor, not-reported or warning. Read it back with 'show alarm-severity-entry-...', which also returns service-affecting (indeterminate, sa, nsa, sa-nsa). Press ? after 'set alarm-severity-entity' to list available entities. The object is system-managed and cannot be manually deleted.

alarm-severity-profile sets the severity for a whole profile entry rather than for one resource-type/alarm-type/direction/location combination. Syntax: 'set alarm-severity-profile <profile-entry> severity <critical|event|major|minor|not-reported|warning>' and 'show alarm-severity-profile'; press ? after 'set alarm-severity-profile' to list available profiles. Example: 'set alarm-severity-profile alarm-severity-entry-trusted-certificate/CERTIFICATE-EXPIRED severity critical'. By contrast alarm-severity-entry is keyed per instance as alarm-severity-entry-<resource-type>/<alarm-type>/<direction>/<location> and also exposes service-affecting on show. Both take the same severity value set, both run in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode, and both objects are managed by the system and cannot be manually deleted.

Use 'show current-alarms [number-of-alarms] [last-changed]'. number-of-alarms is the count of currently raised alarms, and last-changed is the timestamp of the last change in the current alarm list, covering either a raise or a clear event. Access is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode. If you want the count broken down by severity, the system dashboard from the 'status' command reports it, for example '13 current alarms (1 critical, 5 major, 2 not-reported, 5 minor)'. For the alarms themselves use 'show alarms' or 'show alarm-<alarm-id>' with filters.

Look at conditions with the 'get-conditions' command. A condition is an alarm that is not considered current, which happens when the alarm severity is configured as not-reported or not-alarmed, when the alarm is suppressed due to alarm correlation, when it is suppressed due to ARC (alarm reporting control), or when it is suppressed due to AINS. Syntax: 'get-conditions [[direction=]<value>] [[resource=]<value>] [[resource-type=]<value>] [[alarm-type=]<value>] [[location=]<value>] [[AID=]<value>]'. direction takes all, na, ingress or egress and defaults to all; location takes all, na, near-end or far-end and also defaults to all; resource, resource-type, alarm-type and AID have no default. Access is Operational mode.

Use set-alarm-state, which changes the operator state of an alarm and can store user data in the alarm itself. Syntax: set-alarm-state [state=]<value> [[acknowledge-text=]<value>] (all-alarms | [alarm-id-list=]<value>[,<value>]*). The state parameter is mandatory and takes operator-state values none, ack or close. Use all-alarms to set all currently raised alarms, or alarm-id-list to name specific alarms (from 1 up to 10 alarm ids). acknowledge-text is optional and inserts an acknowledge message, string length 0..256. Setting an alarm to its current state is accepted, with only the text being updated. Access Mode: Operational Mode. Example: set-alarm-state ack all-alarms acknowledge-text=example, or set-alarm-state ack 28872914984089790,17580406225060810165.

Yes. The statistics command clears the event counters (statistics) for the specified objects: clear [-f] statistics [target=]<value>[,<value>]*. Access Mode is Operational Mode. Flags: -h displays help, -f forces the command without confirmation. The target parameter is an instance-identifier naming the objects whose event counter statistics are cleared; multiple comma-separated targets are allowed. Scope is limited: currently the only supported object type is aaa-server, and AAA statistics are supported for TACACS+ servers but not for RADIUS servers. Example, clear all AAA servers: clear statistics aaa-server. Clear one server: clear statistics aaa-server-MyServer.

Use show log with the -n and -t flags: show [-n=<number>] [-t] log [<logname> [exclude=<exclude-column> ...]]. -n=x limits output to the last x log entries and -t switches from the default CSV output to an aligned table display. So for the last 5 security entries in table form: show -n=5 log security -t. Valid lognames include messages, linecard, shell-command, netconf-command, apps, cli-command, alarm, configuration, kernel, user, event, security and ztp. If the table becomes too wide, drop columns with exclude=<column> after the logname (use <tab> auto-complete to list removable columns). Output can also be piped, for example show log security | exclude john | include NETCONF. Access Mode: Operational mode, and Candidate Configuration mode for the show command only. Note the security log may not be cleared with clear log.

Yes, that is expected: console logging is off by default. The log-console object has an enabled attribute that switches console logging on and off, with values true or false and a default of false. Turn it on with: set log-console enabled true. Verify with show log-console. The other attribute is source-facilities, the list of syslog facilities used in this configuration, chosen from all, authentication, clock-daemon-15, clock-daemon-9, ftp-daemon, kernel, line-printer, local1 through local7, log-alert, log-audit, mail-system, network-news, ntp, security, syslog-internal, system-daemons, user-level and uucp. Syntax: set log-console [source-facilities <value>] [enabled <value>] / show log-console [source-facilities] [enabled]. Access Mode: Operational mode, Candidate Configuration mode.

Add a log-console-facility-filter, a selector that filters messages by source facility and severity: add log-console-facility-filter-<name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. The <name> identifies a single syslog facility, or all of them if the value is 'all'. severity takes emergency (level 0), alert (1), critical (2), error (3), warning (4), notice (5), informational (6) or debug (7), and defaults to informational. compare-op controls how the comparison is made, with values equals, equals-or-higher or not-equals, default equals-or-higher. To keep informational messages off the console and show only serious ones: add log-console-facility-filter-all severity 'critical'. Use set to change an existing filter, show to view it and delete log-console-facility-filter-<name> to remove it. Access Mode: Operational mode, Candidate Configuration mode.

Local history is bounded by two log-file attributes. max-file-size is the maximum file size before rotation in megabytes, uint8 range 1..30, default 30. number-of-files is the maximum number of log files retained, uint8 range 1..20, default 10: when rotating files because max-file-size is reached, the oldest files are discarded if the total number of files is greater than number-of-files. So by default the node keeps up to 10 files of up to 30 MB each before discarding. Set them with: set log-file-<name> number-of-files <value> max-file-size <value>. The log-file name is the file name without the .log extension, String length 0...128 characters. The default system log file cannot be edited or deleted; locally saved log files can be emptied with clear or removed with delete.

Yes. Create the local file restricted to the authentication facility, then optionally add a severity filter. Use add log-file-<name> [number-of-files <value>] [max-file-size <value>] [source-facilities <string>] [pattern-match <string>] [sensitive-data <value>], setting source-facilities to authentication (the facility used for authentication/authorization attempts messages, RFC facility 4); source-facilities defaults to all. For example: add log-file-authonly source-facilities authentication. To narrow severity, add log-file-facility-filter-<log-file-name>/<log-file-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>], where the filter name identifies a single syslog facility or 'all'; severity defaults to informational and compare-op defaults to equals-or-higher. You can also constrain entries with pattern-match, a regex string of length 0..255.

Configure a log-server: add log-server-<name> address <IP address> ... port <value> transport <udp|tls|tcp>. transport is the transport protocol used when forwarding logs, with values tcp, udp and tls, and it defaults to udp, so you must specify transport tls explicitly. Unless you say otherwise, port defaults to 514 (range 1..65535) and message-format defaults to rfc5424 (the alternative is rfc3164). Other defaults: enabled true, message-coalescence true, source-facilities all, origin manual, sensitive-data none, destination-facility-override disabled, alarm-report-control allowed. address may be IPv4, IPv6 or a DNS domain name; name is a String of length 0...64. Example: add log-server-1 address '10.220.225.165' source-facilities local7.

Yes you can filter per collector, but the filter can only narrow, not widen. Use add log-server-facility-filter-<log-server-name>/<log-server-facility-filter-name> [severity <value>] [compare-op <value>]. The guide states this is a filter based on the source-facilities leaf-list and can only add a filter to the configured source facilities, so it cannot make the server send facilities that are not already in that log-server's source-facilities list. The filter name identifies a single syslog facility, or all of them if the value is 'all', chosen from kernel, user-level, mail-system, system-daemons, authentication, syslog-internal, line-printer, network-news, uucp, clock-daemon-9, security, ftp-daemon, ntp, log-audit, log-alert, clock-daemon-15, local0-local7 and all. severity defaults to informational and compare-op defaults to equals-or-higher (also equals, not-equals). Example: add log-server-facility-filter-server184/local2 severity debug.

Use the syslog remote-logging-switch flag: set syslog remote-logging-switch false. It is described as the flag to enable remote logging switch, and if false it disables all remote logging destinations; values are true or false with a default of true. This leaves the configured log-server entries in place. Related syslog attributes: log-relay (flag to enable remote logging from a shelf controller to a node controller, default false), source-address (default localhost), log-file-message-coalescence (default true), assignment-method (both, manual, dhcp, default both), niap-compliant-logging (default false), privacy-mode (default false), alarm-report-control (allowed or inhibited, default allowed) and label (string 0..256). Check the current setting with show syslog remote-logging-switch. Access Mode: Operational mode, Candidate Configuration mode.

The aaa-server page states that the maximum length of shared-secret is 64 characters, and any value more than 64 characters is denied with an error message. The parameter table lists shared-secret as the shared secret of the aaa server, type String (length 0...128), with default sharedkey; the shared secret is always displayed as * rather than in clear text. Set it with add aaa-server-<server-name> ... [shared-secret <value>] or set aaa-server-<server-name> [shared-secret <value>], and read it back with show aaa-server-<server-name> shared-secret. For reference, the server-name itself is a string of length 1...64. Access Mode: Operational Mode, Candidate Configuration Mode.

That is expected behaviour, not a bug. Under show aaa-statistics-<server-name> authentication-requests, the guide notes that for TACACS+ the default authentication protocol includes both PAP and CHAP, and the authentication requests counter tracks each retry and each authentication protocol attempted independently, so authentication requests may increase by 2 for each retry. The aaa-statistics command applies only to AAA servers that use the TACACS+ protocol. Available counters are connection-failures (failures due to unavailable servers and timeouts), authentication-requests, authentication-rejects, authorization-requests, authorization-rejects and accounting-requests, all integers. Example: show aaa-statistics-tacacs_server1. You can reset the counters with clear statistics aaa-server-<name>.

If you omit action, the ACE drops matching packets: the action parameter, the action taken by the filter, has values drop, accept and reject with a default of drop. Pre-condition: an ACL must be in place before an ACE can be added, and at least one of Source IP, Destination IP, L4 ports, TTL or protocol must be provided. Limits: the sequence-id range is 1-100 for AUX and DCN-B interfaces and 1-256 for the DCN-A interface, and it is recommended to use multiples of 5 so rules can be inserted later. A maximum of 16 ACEs can be created on an ACL if both upper-port and lower-port values are specified; adding a seventeenth such ACE returns an error. Other defaults: direction input, logging-action false, protocol any, ttl 255, source/destination lower and upper port 0. Example: add ace-TrafficV6/100 action drop source-ip-address 2420::5.

An ACL is bound to one management interface at creation: add acl-<name> type <value> interface <value> [admin-state <value>]. The available interfaces are 1-AUX-1, 1-AUX-2, DCN, DCN-B, DCN-2 and DCN-2-B (use add acl-name interface ? to list them). Yes, IPv6 is handled: the type parameter indicates the top-level type of ACL, that is which fields from the associated IPv4 or IPv6 headers the ACL matches on, with values IPv4 and IPv6, and it is mandatory on add. name is a string of length 0...30 and admin-state takes lock, maintenance or unlock, default unlock. An ACL can have one or more ACEs. Note: an ACL can be added on the DCN-B interface when the DCN is operating in active-active configuration. Example: add acl-AuxV4traffic interface 1-AUX-2 type ipv4.

Yes: show access-control-list. It is a show-only command used to display the access control list, it takes no parameters, and its Access Mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. To work with individual lists and their entries instead, use the acl commands (add/set/show/delete acl-<name>, with type, interface, admin-state, oper-state and avail-state) and the ace commands (add/set/show/delete ace-<name>/<sequence-id>) for each access control entry within an ACL.

Create an access-rule-list bound to that group, then add a deny rule for the path. First: add access-rule-list-<name> [user-group <value>] [sequence-id <value>] [description <value>], for example add access-rule-list-A user-group XY. Then: add access-rule-<access-rule-list-name>/<access-rule-name> action <value> [sequence-id <value>] [module-name <value>] [path <value>] [attribute <value>] [attribute-value <value>] [operation <value>] [description <value>]. action is mandatory whenever a rule is created and takes permit or deny. path is the target object, an XPath of a YANG data node, notification, RPC or descendant, or an external command, max length 255, default *. operation is a bits value from create, read, update, delete and execute, default * (all). Example, deny card creation: add access-rule-1/rule path /ne/equipment/card operation create action deny. The system supports a maximum of 500 access-rules across all access-rule-lists.

Order is by sequence-id: the access-rule-list is processed in order as given by the sequence-id parameter, and lower number ids are processed first, so the lowest sequence-id wins first. sequence-id is a uint16 and can be changed over the lifetime of the list to re-sort entries; if you do not provide it, it is set to the currently used latest id plus 1, that is the entry goes to the end of the list. The same sequence-id rule applies to individual access-rules within a list. To say which groups a list applies to, use the user-group parameter: add access-rule-list-<name> [user-group <value>] [sequence-id <value>] [description <value>]. user-group is a leaf-list of user-group names or '*', defaulting to '*' as a match-all meaning the list applies to all existing user-groups; a maximum of 20 user-groups can be referenced. Example: add access-rule-list-A user-group XY.

Despite the generic name, auth-key is OSPF-specific: it configures the pre-shared key for OSPFv3 IPsec integrity protection. The AID is scoped entirely by OSPF: add auth-key-<instance-id>/<ospf-area-id>/<ospf-if-name>/<spi> key <value> [type <value>], with matching set, show and delete forms. instance-id is the OSPF instance ID, a number in range 0..255; ospf-area-id is the OSPF Router Area ID (string); ospf-if-name is a reference to the interface in the OSPF area; and spi is a unique security parameter index for this SA, a number in range 256..4294967295. key is a string of length 8..128, and type indicates whether the integrity key is ASCII or hexadecimal encoded, values ascii or hex. Example: add auth-key-1/0.0.0.0/DCN/256 key abcdefgh12345678. Access Mode: Operational mode, Candidate Configuration mode.

Set the global authorization mode to rules-only: set authorization mode rules-only. mode selects which kind of authorization rules are used, with values static-only (only system defined static authorization rules), static+rules (both user and system defined access-rules, the system tries a user configured access-rule first and falls back to system rules) and rules-only (only user defined access-rules; if no rule matches, the global defaults are used). The default is static+rules. In rules-only mode the fallbacks are read-default, write-default and exec-default, each permit or deny and only configurable when mode = rules-only; their defaults are read-default permit, write-default deny, exec-default permit. To deny everything the rules do not cover, set all three to deny, for example set authorization write-default deny. show authorization also reports denied-operations, denied-data-writes and denied-notifications counters since the last restart.

Every user changes their own password with the password command: password [old-password=<old-password>] [new-password=<new-password>]. Both the current/old password and the new password are required, and this is supported only for local users. A password may contain up to 200 characters. Input can be inline, as normal parameters that are not hidden from view and are usable in scripts, or interactive, where the passwords are prompted for and not echoed and the new one must be typed twice; interactive input can be cancelled with Ctrl+C. Inline, special characters \"' must be escaped with \\ and #?|; must be enclosed in quotes. Example: password old-password=Infinera4u! new-password=Infinera4us!. To reset another user's password as an admin, use set user-<username> force-password-change true, which forces the user to change their password on next login. Access Mode for password: Operational mode.

Use show security. It is the command that shows the top level security container, it takes no parameters, and its Access Mode is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: show security. For the individual settings underneath it, use show security-policies for the security policy flags (secure-mode, strict-password-check, minimum-password-length, ssh and TLS algorithm lists, and so on), show access-control-list for ACLs, and show user-group, show user or show user-data for the user side.

Minimum password length is governed by minimum-password-length under security-policies: a configurable minimum length for user passwords, number in range 1..200, default 8; the length is verified against this policy whenever a password is changed. strict-password-check (true/false, default true) additionally enforces a minimum length of 8 characters, at least one lower case letter (a-z), at least one upper case letter (A-Z), at least one number (0-9), at least one symbol, and that the user name cannot be part of the password; if disabled, only a minimum length of 1 character applies. For password reuse, enforce-password-history-check (true/false, default true) ensures a new password cannot match any of the previous 5 passwords, and password-history-size sets the number of passwords stored for reuse checking, number in range 1..200, default 5. Both history and strictness policies affect only newly defined passwords once enabled.

Lockout is per user, on the user object. max-invalid-login is the maximum number of consecutive invalid login attempts before an account is suspended (locked out), a number in range 0-255 with a default of 5. suspension-time is the duration of UID suspension following consecutive invalid login attempts, in minutes, range 0 - 1440, default 5 minutes. So by default 5 failed logins lock the account for 5 minutes. Set them with add user-<user-name> [max-invalid-login <value>] [suspension-time <value>] or the equivalent set. show user-<user-name> reports failed-logins, the number of previous failed logins, which resets to zero upon a successful login, and user-status, where the value lockout means the account is locked out due to unsuccessful login attempts. Lockout can also be turned off globally with the security-policies disable-user-lockout attribute.

user-data is a show-only command: show user-data. The guide states the commands in that section are used to show the user-data, its Access Mode is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode, and its Command Parameters section is None, so it takes no arguments and no per-attribute selectors. For per-user attributes such as user-group, max-invalid-login, suspension-time, timeout, password-aging-interval, password-expiration-date, user-status, last-login-date, failed-logins and user-aaa-type, use show user-<user-name> instead.

Use add user-group-<name> [description <value>]. Each user is associated with a list of groups and derives its permissions from them. name is the name of the group, a String of 1...64 characters, and description is a long description of the user group, a String of 1...128 characters. The matching commands are set user-group-<name> [description <value>], show user-group-<name> [description] and delete user-group-<name>. Access Mode: Operational mode, Candidate Configuration mode. Example: add user-group-XY, then delete user-group-XY to remove it. show user-group lists the built-in groups: EA Encryption Administrator, MA Monitoring Access, NA Network Administrator, NE Network Engineer, PR Provisioning, SA Security Administrator and TT Turn-up and Test. Assign groups to a user with add user-<user-name> user-group <value>, and reference groups from an access-rule-list with its user-group parameter.

Add/Drop Groups are identified by adg-number, an integer in the range [1..110], so a node can have up to 110 ADGs. Use 'add adg-<adg-number>' to create one, 'set adg-<adg-number> label <value>' to label it (String 0..256), and 'delete adg-<adg-number>' to remove it. Whether the same wavelength may appear twice is reported by the read-only (show) attribute wavelength-duplication: 'one-per-adg' (the default) means no duplication of frequencies in the ADG, and 'one-per-degree' means duplication of frequencies is allowed in the ADG but only one at the Degree. Only CDCs allow more than one instance of the same wavelength on the ADG. Other show attributes are max-add-drop-ports (max ports for the ADG) and bands-supported, default standardC-band. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On 'set amplifier-<name>', gain-target sets the constant-gain value over 0..40 dB, default 0.0, and applies only in manual control-mode. control-mode is auto-max-pw (default, the auto mode targeting maximum output power) or manual; amp-control-support shows whether auto-max-pw is permitted ('auto') or 'manual-only'. In auto mode you instead use gain-adjustment, a user offset in [-20.00..20.00] dB, default 0, supported only on amplifiers with function 'pa' or 'inline'. gain-operating reports the actually configured gain (0.0 when the card is out or the EDFA disabled). Tilt is controlled by tilt-control-mode: 'auto' (default) has the system implicitly control tilt per configured fiber parameters, 'auto-planned' per planning tool parameters, and 'manual' lets the user control it. tilt-target ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) applies in manual mode and raises a warning that the attribute may be traffic affecting; tilt-adjustment ([-5..5] dB, default 0dB) offsets the target when mode is auto or auto-planned. When amplifier function is 'add' or 'drop', the only tilt option is 'manual'.

Use 'set amplifier-raman-<name> target-raman-gain <value>'. The permitted range is [0, 5..30dB] with a default of 0dB. It is configurable only when control-mode is different than auto; if control-mode is 'auto' the parameter is ignored. control-mode values are auto (default; you configure only the span attributes and optionally the pointloss, gain is automatically controlled), auto-planned (you configure the target Raman gain plus span attributes), and manual (basic manual configuration, where even the target pump powers must be configured). To see how many pumps the card has, use 'show amplifier-raman-<name> number-of-pumps'; the values are 4 or 2, and this value dictates the number of pump-power objects exposed by the system. Related read-outs are total-pump-power ([-99..99 dBm], -99 means no power), actual-raman-signal-gain and actual-raman-osc-gain (both 0 when the Raman amplifier or card is disabled).

Switch it on with 'set ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-enable enabled', for example 'set ase-idler-service-1-8 ase-idler-enable enabled'. The default is disabled; enabled means ASE idler signal filling on the unused and nmc-failed portions of the band spectrum is enabled. The entity can also be created with the value in place: 'add ase-idler-service-<name> [alarm-report-control <value>] [ase-idler-enable <value>]', and removed with 'delete ase-idler-service-<name>'. To see whether it actually came up, read the ase-idler-state attribute with 'show ase-idler-service-<name> ase-idler-state': ase-enabled (filling complete on the band spectrum), ase-partially-enabled (filling incomplete), ase-faulted (signal faulted), or ase-disabled (default, signal completely removed from the band spectrum). oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled) and avail-state are also available; function is 'idler'.

target-output-power is the ASE pump output power required when manually configured, with a range of (-3.00..20.50) dBm and a default of 13. The pump is not on by default: pump-enable (enabled/disabled) defaults to disabled, and the read-only pump-state, which reports the state of the ASE Idler pump, also defaults to disabled. Both are set with 'set ase-idler-source-<name>', for example 'set ase-idler-source-1-3.1-ase pump-enable 'enabled' target-output-power '15.00''. Other settable attributes are admin-state (lock, unlock, maintenance; default unlock), label (String 0..256) and alarm-report-control (allowed by default, or inhibited). function is fixed at ase-idler-source. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use the 'calibrate' command, whose syntax is 'calibrate [type=]<value> [trigger=]<value> [entity=]<value>'. type has the single value 'raman', which triggers calibration on Raman cards. trigger is 'start' to start the Raman gain calibration for the OTS span, or 'stop' to stop it. entity selects the entity to be calibrated as an instance-identifier; for Raman calibration the entity may be an OTS-R entity. So to kick one off: 'calibrate raman start ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line', and to stop it: 'calibrate raman stop ots-r-1-1-dwdm-line'. None of the three parameters has a default. The command is available in Operational Mode only.

A degree is identified by degree-number, an integer in the range [1..20], and the number must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees, so a node can have up to 20 degrees. Manage them with 'add degree-<degree-number>', 'set degree-<degree-number> label <value>', 'delete degree-<degree-number>' and 'show degree-<degree-number>'. For spectral granularity, the show attributes are slot-width-granularity, the width of a slot given in MHz, default 6250, and center-freq-granularity, the granularity of allowed center frequencies in MHz, default 3125, computed from a base frequency of 193.1 THz (G.694.1). Slots are joined to form a media channel between min-slots (default 8) and max-slots (default 32), where min-slots must be less than or equal to max-slots. bands-supported defaults to standardC-band.

On a multi-rail ILA node, direction n and direction n+1 are automatically assigned by the system to the DWDM Line1 and DWDM Line2 ports of the #n C2ILASGH/D2ILASGM card created, where index n is an odd integer with a value between 1 and 15. That is why they come in pairs: the DWDM Line1 port is always assigned an odd index value and the DWDM Line2 port is always assigned an even index value. The direction index range is [1..16] (1 and 2 are used when migrating from R6.x). The system sets direction-number from the configured direction-port: 1 when the port is dwdm-line1 and 2 when it is dwdm-line2, and it fills direction-card (card-<chassis>-<slot>) autonomously. The same dwdm-line* port instance of an ILAx can only be selected once per NE. Syntax: 'add direction-<index> direction-port <value> [label <value>]', with 'delete [-f] direction-<index>' forcing without confirmation.

On a dsc facility you can configure only three attributes, using 'add dsc-<name>' or 'set dsc-<name>': label (String 0..256), admin-state (lock, unlock or maintenance, default unlock), and alarm-report-control (allowed, the default, or inhibited). Everything else is show-only: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by. The managed-by attribute describes whether the facility was system created or not; its values are 'system' and 'user' with a default of 'system'. It matters because only user-created facilities can be user deleted, so a dsc reporting managed-by 'system' cannot be removed with 'delete dsc-<name>'. Access is Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On 'add dsc-group-<name>' or 'set dsc-group-<name>' there are two Q signal-degrade thresholds with matching hysteresis. Pre-FEC: pre-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold raises the PRE-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE alarm, decimal64 with fraction-digits 3, range 0|5.600..9.600 dB, where 0 implies threshold crossing alarming is disabled and the specific sub-range is per carrier use-case; pre-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is decimal64 fraction-digits 1, range 0.1..1.0 dB, default 0.5. Post-FEC: post-fec-q-sig-deg-threshold raises POST-FEC-Q-SIGNAL-DEGRADE, decimal64 fraction-digits 1, range (12.5..18.0) dB, default 18; post-fec-q-sig-deg-hysteresis is range (0.1..1.0) dB, default 0.5. Alongside these, dgd-high-threshold raises the DGD-OORH alarm, uint16 range (25..400) ps, default 100.

Use the 'gadt' command, which retrieves golden carrier application information: 'show gadt [<application-description-H|application-description-P|application-description-S|application-description-U>]'. Each of the four parameters, application-description-H, application-description-P, application-description-S and application-description-U, is a string giving the detailed description of that application ID, and none has a default. For example, 'show gadt application-description-H' returns application-description 'Subsea modes using Uniform and Hybrid modulation'. Running 'show gadt' without a parameter lists them all. The command is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

The 'gapt' command lists the golden advanced parameters from the Golden Advanced Parameters Table (GAPT). It is scoped per card type: the syntax is 'show gapt-<card-type> [version] [applicable-resource-type]', where card-type is a card type name string, version is the table version (string, length 0..5), and applicable-resource-type is the managed resource type(s) applicable for that particular advanced parameter. Plain 'show gapt' lists the tables and their versions, for example gapt-CHM6 version 1.8, gapt-CHM7 version 3.0, and gapt-CHM7T. Scoping to one card, 'show gapt-chm7', lists that card's parameters as golden-advanced-parameter-CHM7/<name> entries such as BOASetting, CRAvgNCtrl, ClockPreEmphasis, EEPNNLMitigation, NLC, PDLMitigation, RxCDMode, RxRollOff and TxSignalBWControl, followed by the table version. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use the 'gcmt' command, which retrieves information about the golden carrier mode. The syntax is 'show gcmt [<card-type>] [version]', where the object parameter is the golden carrier modes string and version is the table version. To look up one specific mode, name it directly: 'show gcmt golden-carrier-mode-800M.95P'. The output lists the resolved mode with its per-card qualification and the mode's characteristics, for example golden-carrier-mode-CHM6/800M.95P with capacity 800 Gbps, client-mode ethernet-otn, baud-rate 95.2965203 GBaud, application P, compatibility-id 6, and status supported. The command is available in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Read the status attribute with 'show golden-carrier-mode-<card-type>/<carrier-mode> status'. status describes the carrier mode release status and its values are supported, candidate, experimental, deprecated and diagnostic, so a mode reading 'supported' is fully supported while 'experimental' is not. Two related attributes qualify this per subtype: supported-subtypes lists the subtypes each carrier mode supports (string length 0..32, maximum 20 elements), and candidate-subtypes lists the subtypes for which this carrier mode has candidate status (string length 0..16, maximum 10 elements). The carrier-mode key is a string of 1..15 characters in the format <Capacity><ClientMode>.<Baud Rate><Application ID>, for example 600E.84P, 100X.73U or 325M.66P. Other readable attributes include actual-carrier-mode, capacity (Gbps), client-mode (ethernet, ethernet-otn), baud-rate, application, compatibility-id and sop-tracking-mode.

The 'l0-capabilities' command shows the capabilities details related with the node's Layer 0 functions. The syntax is simply 'show l0-capabilities'; the command takes no parameters at all. It is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode. For the OADM-specific limits, the separate 'oadm-capabilities' command reports max-degrees and max-adgs.

To carve out a Media Channel you must supply three mandatory arguments: 'add mc-<name> parent-oms <value> lower-frequency <value> upper-frequency <value>', optionally followed by [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [auto-delete <value>]. lower-frequency and upper-frequency are the lower and upper frequencies of the Media Channel, given in MHz. parent-oms is an instance-identifier that is only set upon MC creation, and the referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree, it cannot be in an ADG. The system then derives center-frequency (in MHz) and slot-width, calculated as upper-frequency minus lower-frequency. auto-delete defaults to disabled; when enabled the system auto-deletes the MC once its associated NMC is deleted, and it may only be enabled on RD66TM sleds (l0-mode-op=hsc-ols), always being disabled if l0-mode-op is standard or slte. Example: 'add mc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 parent-oms '1-3.1-dwdm-line' lower-frequency '192225000' upper-frequency '192300000''.

The Media Channel Filler is read only. The 'mc-f' command is used only to show the Media Channel Filler facility attributes, and the sole syntax is 'show mc-f-<name> [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [AID] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [slot-width]'. There is no add, set or delete form. Every parameter is listed as used in 'show' only: name (String 0..64), supporting-facilities and supported-facilities (instance identifiers to the parent and children facilities), supporting-card, supporting-port, AID (String 1..64), lower-frequency and upper-frequency of the MC Filler in MHz units, and slot-width, which the system calculates from upper-frequency minus lower-frequency in MHz units. None of these has a default. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Up to four cards per ADG: in 'add modules-adg-<adg-number>/<index> supported-card <value> [ocm-monitoring <value>]', the index is a number in the range [1..4], and adg-number is in the range [1..110]. The card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is the card instance identifier. Channel monitoring is on by default: ocm-monitoring has values true and false with a default of true. It is set upon creation and cannot be changed after supported-card has been assigned; it can optionally be configured to false for OMD cards directly connected to PAx/BAX or C2ILASGH degrees, for example FOADM nodes. Example: 'add modules-adg-1/1 supported-card card-1-6'. Access requires Network Administrator or Network Engineer privilege, in Operational mode or Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use the 'modules-degree' command: 'add modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>'. degree-number is a number in the range [1..20] and must be greater than zero and not greater than max-degrees. index has the single permitted value 1, since the card with index 1 must be the card, subcard or module fibered to the Degree(s). supported-card is the instance identifier of the card or subcard that belongs to the degree; in R6.0 the card must be RD09SM or RD20TM. You can later change it with 'set modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card <value>', inspect it with 'show modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index> supported-card', and remove the association with 'delete modules-degree-<degree-number>/<index>'. Example: 'add modules-degree-1/1 supported-card card-1-1'. Requires Network Administrator or Network Engineer privilege, in Operational mode or Candidate Configuration Mode.

Use 'show monitored-channel-<name>/<frequency> monitored-optical-power'. The name corresponds to the (WS04S) card name with the suffix -1 or -2, for ocm1-in or ocm2-in respectively, and frequency is the nominal center frequency of the carrier (channel) in MHz as a uint32. monitored-optical-power is the measured power for that carrier in dBm, decimal64 with range (-99.00..99.00) and default -99, where the value -99.00 means no power. The companion attribute monitored-width (uint32, default 0) gives the carrier width configured at the NMC within the oxcon source/destination, in MHz. Example: 'show monitored-channel-1-1.2-ocm1-in/195987500 monitored-optical-power', or omit the attribute to see all attributes of that channel. The command is show-only, in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

center-frequency is the nominal center frequency of the NMC and takes values in the range [190650000..196700000] MHz. It is mandatory on creation: 'add nmc-<name> parent-facility <value> center-frequency <value>'. width is the Network Media Channel frequency width in MHz, with values in the range [15000..200000] MHz and a default of 35000. The user must configure the 3 dB signal bandwidth, and the value in GHz must be equivalent to the baud rate (GBd) configured on the connected transponder line interface line port. Both center-frequency and width are used in add and show only, so they are fixed at creation and not changeable with 'set'. parent-facility can be either a Media Channel or an OMS, is only set upon creation, and its referenced supporting-card must be part of a Degree, not an ADG. Example: 'add nmc-cdc-1-4_192800000-34000 center-frequency 192800000 width 34000 parent-facility oms-1-4-ad1'.

The Network Media Channel Filler occupies an allocated bandwidth of 75000 MHz by default: alloc-bandwidth is a value in MHz units with a default of 75000, bounded by alloc-lower-frequency and alloc-upper-frequency. What is currently in use is reported separately by actual-bandwidth, in MHz units with a default of 0, together with actual-lower-frequency and actual-upper-frequency. It is monitored: monitoring-state indicates whether the NMC is intended to be in use, and because this is a system created attribute it is enabled by default, values enabled and disabled. Power read-outs are power-actual-tx and power-actual-rx, both [-99.00..99.00] dBm with default -99, plus output-attenuation-compensation-actual (decimal64, fraction-digits 2, range -20..20, default 0). Only admin-state and alarm-report-control are settable via 'set nmc-f-<name>'.

Use 'show oadm-capabilities [max-degrees] [max-adgs]'. max-degrees is the maximum number of degrees, reported as 20 (uint8), and max-adgs is the maximum number of Add/Drop Groups, reported as 110 (uint8); either is 0 if not supported. Degrees and ADGs are only supported in OADM node types, and the maximum degrees for the ILA node-type is 0 by convention because an ILA has only 2 directions, fixedly, which is not shown in supported capabilities. Note that the maximum number of Degrees is not necessarily the deployment supported configuration, but the maximum number of a working degree-number. Sample output: 'show oadm-capabilities' returns max-degrees 20 and max-adgs 110. The command is show-only, in Operational mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

On 'set oc-<name>' the loopback attribute takes facility, terminal or none, with a default of none, and is useful to debug on the fiber connection; loopback-mode indicates the loopback action for facility or terminal and takes facility or terminal. For test patterns, test-signal-type is the type of test pattern that is injected and takes none (the default), enumeration, PRBS31Q, PRBS13Q, scrambled-idles, PRBS9 or PRBS31. test-signal-direction takes the single value ingress, which is also the default. test-signal-monitoring monitors the incoming test signals for diagnostics and takes true or false, defaulting to false. Example: 'set oc-1-5-T9.1 test-signal-monitoring false'. All of these are readable back with 'show oc-<name>'. Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

In ILA nodes the OCHm represents the signaled optical channel from OSC, detected at the ILA OMS by using the OSC information. Consequently, when either the OMS monitoring-mode is 'not-monitored' as configured by the user, or there is no OSC messaging information, the list of OCHm facilities in the NE will be empty. Inspect it with 'show ochm' or 'show ochm-<name>'. The direction attribute is ingress or egress, but currently only egress is supported and it is the default. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, where -99dBm means either that the power is not yet measured, measurement being performed by the OCM at the DGE2 card, or that no power was detected or there is no appropriate fiber-connection; for the egress direction the power actual should be calibrated at the DWDM Line port output, at the same reference point where the target power is defined. target-actual-power (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99) and attenuation-actual (0..55 dB, the DGE VOA attenuation of the channel) apply to HSC OLS nodes. Only label, admin-state and alarm-report-control are settable.

Use the ocm-channel facility: show ocm-channel-<name>/<lower-frequency>/<upper-frequency> [opm-pwr] [connected]. It lists the detected carriers within the configured OXcon(s). name is a String (length 0..64); lower-frequency and upper-frequency are uint32 and give the lower/upper frequency of the corresponding spectrum power (OPM-pwr point); opm-pwr is the Optical Parameter Monitor power in dBm, decimal64 range -99.00..99.00 with default -99; connected yields 'true' if the channel is configured, i.e. involved in an oxcon, values true/false with default false. ocm-channel is show-only and is available in Operational Mode and Candidate Configuration Mode.

Yes. On ocm-mp the ocm-enable attribute, which enables regular power monitoring, takes values disabled or enabled and defaults to enabled. Configure it with set ocm-mp-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [ocm-enable <value>] - those three are the only settable attributes besides the name. The related read-only monitoring-state also defaults to enabled: the system reports 'enabled' when an OMS reference exists. Other show-only attributes include monitored-port (the port being monitored, can differ from supporting-port for a non-integrated OCM, default not-applicable) and ad-direction, which for ocm-mp only takes the value ingress. admin-state defaults to unlock and managed-by is system. Access: Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode.

The ocm-ptp facility is available for WS04S cards within a CD-AD ADG and provides dedicated OCM monitoring. It is not on by default: ocm-enable (enables regular power monitoring) takes enabled or disabled and defaults to disabled, so you must turn it on, for example set ocm-ptp-1-1.2-ocm1-in ocm-enable enabled. Settable attributes are label, admin-state (lock/unlock/maintenance, default unlock) and ocm-enable. Read-only: ad-direction (egress or ingress, default ingress), last-measurement (date-and-time or never, default never), adg-number (uint8, range 0..110, default 0), and monitoring-state, which defaults to disabled and reports 'enabled' only when complete connectivity at the AD is established and OCM measurement is possible.

On the oms facility, grid-mode defaults to flexible. Permitted values: flexible, fixed-50G-96ch, fixed-100G-48ch, fixed-75G-64ch, fixed-75G-64ch-oif, fixed-50G-7100 (88 channels, set automatically when osc-compatibility is osc-7100) and fixed-150G-40ch. Default spectrum limits are lower-frequency 191300000 and upper-frequency 196150000 (191.3 to 196.15 THz, standardC-band). monitoring-mode selects how the section is monitored: not-monitored (non-intrusive monitoring, no OCM/DGE required), intrusive (TTP), non-intrusive (CTP, operates with OCM e.g. DGE), dge-fixed-attenuation (fixed attenuation due to a connected interstage device), ila-with-equalization (operates with DGE and OCM) and integrated-equalization (integrated DGE). Default is intrusive for all node types except ILA, not-monitored for ILA, and integrated-equalization for hyperscale ILA nodes. It is only exposed for an OMS of a port that belongs to a degree, or on an ILA node.

set ops-<name> accepts label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, input-psd-profile, role and port-expansion. input-psd-profile is the nominal expected tributary channel power density in dBm/12.5GHz, decimal64 range -30..-6, default -6. role is one of tributary (single add/drop to a local or remote transponder), multi-carrier (multiple carriers on the underlying filter port), general-purpose (other cases, e.g. express cross-connection to another filter), ase-input (only on specific RD ports in SLTE l0-mode-op) and active-multi-carrier (multiple carriers with active port control); default is general-purpose. port-expansion is no or y-cable, default no, intended for Y-cable expansion. supported-roles is read-only and shows which roles the card, and sometimes the card-mode, allows. Example: set ops-1-6-ad1 role tributary.

On optical-carrier, frequency is the center frequency, range 0 | 191275000..196125000 MHz (0 means not configured), with the usable sub-range set by module and pluggable: CHM7 and CHM7X 190625000-196725000 MHz step 50 MHz, CHM6 191333000-196117000 MHz step 50 MHz, CHM2TX 191292500-196137500 MHz step 1 MHz, CHM1R with TOM-400G-C-DWDM 191275000-196125000 MHz with fine tune. tx-power is the transmit power into the fiber, range -55.0..55.00 dBm with accuracy adjustable in steps of 0.5 dBm and per-module limits, for example CHM2TX -6 to 0 (default 0), CHM7/CHM7X -10 to 0 (default -2), UTM2 default -6.0, CHM1R with TOM-400G-C-DWDM -10 to 1 (default 1). For a slight trim use frequency-offset, int16 range -6000..6000 MHz, default 0: once set, the frequency changes slowly over 1-10 s without affecting service.

Yes, with propagate-shutdown on the optical-carrier facility: when set, the transmit laser will be shut down if the whole service of that direction has signal failure. The function is mainly used in a regeneration node to propagate signal failure as LOS. Values are enabled and disabled, default disabled. The companion propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer sets the hold off time of propagate shutdown, range 0..2000 milliseconds, default 0. Restriction: neither propagate-shutdown nor propagate-shutdown-holdoff-timer is configurable on the SPN2 or SPN2C card. Example form: set optical-carrier-1-1-1 propagate-shutdown enabled.

Very little. The only settable attributes are label and admin-state: set optical-channel-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>]. label is a String of length 0..256; admin-state takes lock, unlock or maintenance and defaults to unlock. Everything else is read-only through show optical-channel-<name>: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled, default disabled), avail-state and managed-by (system or user, default system; only user-created facilities can be user deleted). Access is Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode. Example: set optical-channel-channel1 admin-state unlock.

Read laser-state on the optical-ptp facility: it reports the emitting pump (for example booster) laser state, values disabled or enabled, default disabled, and is show-only. It is only of relevance for DWDM line ports; on RD amplifiers it means the source (Tx) pump is disabled, on Raman modules it refers to the pump laser and the actual traffic emitted from the dwdm-line port. Yes, you can add fixed pad on receive: fix-rx-attenuation is a settable fixed attenuator before port Rx, decimal64 with 2 fraction digits, range 0..30 dB, default 0, where 0 dB means no fixed attenuator. Example: set -f optical-ptp-1-6-dwdm fix-rx-attenuation 10. The matching fix-tx-attenuation (0..30 dB, default 0) is only visible when ops.port-expansion=y-cable is configured. Measured powers appear in power-actual-rx and power-actual-tx (-99.00..99.00 dBm, default -99).

The Signal Fail decision uses working-los-threshold for the Working Path and protection-los-threshold for the Protection Path. Both are settable optical power in the range -55.0 to 0 dBm and default to -23 dBm. Signal Degrade uses working-switch-threshold and protection-switch-threshold, same -55.0 to 0 dBm range, default -18 dBm, and SD-based switching only happens when switch-threshold-enable is enabled (default disabled). facility-los-threshold sets the facility port threshold below which loss of signal is declared, range -55 to 15 dBm, default -30.0 dBm. Hysteresis is configurable: los-threshold-hysteresis (SF) defaults to 3 dB and switch-threshold-hysteresis (SD) to 2 dB, both range 0.5 to 5.0 dB in 0.1 dB steps, with 1 dB recommended for MCHP and OMSP deployments.

set osc-<name> accepts label, admin-state, alarm-report-control, l0-comm-interface-type, osc-control, target-output-power, tx-power-adjustment, voa-attenuation-target-rx and lof-soak-timer. osc-control is auto or manual, default auto; HSC OLS nodes only support auto. target-output-power is the OSC Tx power at the DWDM line port output, either na or a value in [-2.5..4.5] dBm, default na. tx-power-adjustment trims the automatically calculated Tx power target in osc-control auto mode, na or [-6..6] dB, default 0. voa-attenuation-target-rx is the target Rx VOA in manual control mode, [0..30] dB, default 10. l0-comm-interface-type is ipv4 or ipv6, ipv4 for standard OLS and ipv6 for SLTE and HSC OLS. lof-soak-timer is short (about 3 ms) or long (18,400 OC-3 frames, about 2300 ms), default short, applicable only to the PBAx card. Read-only: osc-mode, osc-wavelength, voa-attenuation-actual-rx, power-actual-rx/tx.

Read otdr-state on the otdr facility: show otdr-<name> otdr-state. Values are not-available (status not available), idle, measuring (measurement is ongoing), finished (measurement has completed) and fail (measurement has failed); default not-available, and a status change triggers a change notification. Supporting read-only attributes: otdr-measurement-time gives the time remaining in the current measurement (default 0), otdr-error carries the error message produced when the measurement ends with error, otdr-laser-state shows the laser as not-available/enabled/disabled, otdr-measurement-port gives the port under measurement (0 means the card is not measuring any port), otdr-measurement-direction is not-available/tx/rx, and otdr-ongoing-measurement-profile shows none, short, medium, long, or raman-precheck1/2/3. Example: show otdr.

On otdr-ptp: otdr-range sets the distance range used to calculate the measurement repetition period, auto or [0...300.0 km], default auto; set it to the fiber length plus 10 percent. From R9.1, if the OTS can be traced through the fiber connection between the ILA/ROADM card and OTDR8OFP2, auto is derived from OTS fiber-length-tx/fiber-length-rx with 10 percent margin rounded up to the nearest 10 km. otdr-resolution is the data sampling resolution, auto or [0.4...100.0], default auto. otdr-pulse-width is auto or [10...20,000 ns], default auto. otdr-measurement-speed is fast (about 10 s), medium (about 15 s), slow (about 1 minute), precision (3 to 5 minutes), high-precision (5 to 7 minutes) or auto, default auto. otdr-ior is auto or [1.0...2.0]. peak-power is auto or [5...14.5]. launching-fiber-length is [0...50 m], default 0, and auto is not supported.

On the ots facility. Fiber type: fiber-type-tx and fiber-type-rx, both default SSMF, chosen from AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS, VistaCor (rx also allows not-applicable, auto and not-configured). Length: fiber-length-tx and fiber-length-rx, auto or [0..500.0] km, default auto, required for tilt control and for Raman backward pumping. Loss: span-loss-transmit and span-loss-receive, decimal64 2 fraction digits, range 0..80 dB (rx also 99 dB), default 0; 0 and 99 dB count as not configured for rx and changing span-loss-receive is traffic affecting. Extra loss such as patch panels goes in external-attenuation-tx/external-attenuation-rx, 0..30 dB, default 0. span-loss-reference (configured or measured, default measured) selects which source power control uses; span-loss-aging-margin-rx is 0.00..10.00 dB, default 1.0.

The ots-diagnostics name is auto generated by the system on line card provisioning. The format is 'ots-diagnostics-<chassis>-<slot>-<DWDM Line>', for example show ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line for an RD20TM DWDM line terminating an OTS section, or ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line1 and ots-diagnostics-1-1-dwdm-line2 for C2ILASGH which terminates two lines. Only nmoper-alarm-reporting (disabled/enabled, default disabled; when enabled a mismatch between expected-operator and rx-operator raises the NMOPER alarm) and expected-operator (up to 32 characters) are settable. tx-operator is also defaulted by the system, with format '<ne-name>-<Dxx>', default <ne-name>-D00. tti-style, rx-operator and tti-port-id are read-only.

On ots-r, required-fiber-type-rx defaults to SSMF. It is the required fiber type on the DWDM Line for the Rx fiber and is only of relevance if control-mode = auto and there is no fiber-connection; the choices are AllWave, DrakaLL, DSF, LEAF, LS, PSLC, PureSilica, SMF-ULL, SSMF, Teralight, TWC, TWMinus, TWPlus, TWReach, TWRS and VistaCor. Other settable receive-span attributes: fiber-length-rx (unspecified or 0..500.0, default unspecified), span-loss-receive (the span loss at the receiving dwdm-line, default 99), external-attenuation-rx (user configured external attenuation), delta-pointloss (additional Rx attenuation determined after turning up pumps, e.g. a bad splice at dwdm-line Rx: not-applicable or -1..3.5 dB, default not-applicable), plus label, admin-state and alarm-report-control. Read-only: configured-fiber-type-rx, configured-fiber-length-rx, span-loss-at-amplifier, power-actual-rx and connected-reference.

Yes, and it does depend on that. The automatic-otdr attribute on ots-r-auto-otdr enables or disables OTDR based automatic fiber check; values enabled and disabled, with default enabled for green field deployments and disabled for in-field SW upgrade. If the Raman card is associated with a base card equipped with integrated OTDR the default is enabled; if the NE has a Raman card that is not aggregated with the EDFA card the value is disabled. The setting persists over warm/cold restart and over SW upgrade. Disabling it while a test is running aborts the ongoing OTDR test and releases the amplifier that the automatic OTDR had blocked; disabling with no test running means no further tests are triggered until re-enabled. Progress is shown by auto-otdr-state: not-applicable, not-available, pass, in-progress, fail, aborted. loss-calibration-by-otdr is none (green field), rx-only, tx-only or tx-rx, default none. Example: set ots-r-auto-otdr-1-1-dwdm-line automatic-otdr enabled.

Use add oxcon-<name> source <value> destination <value> [label] [activation-mode] [auto-delete] [activation-request-fwd] [activation-request-bwd] [direction] [target-output-power-src] [target-output-power-dst] [circuit-id], with the two media channels as source and destination, for example: add oxcon-1-80-192262500__1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500 source 'nmc-1-80-192262500' destination 'nmc-1-3.1-dwdm-line-192262500'. direction is two-way or one-way, default two-way. Whether it comes up by itself depends on activation-mode: automatic means the service is activated automatically by the system on creation and deactivated automatically on deletion, and it is the default in the standard L0 mode of operation; manual (default in SLTE mode) and activate-on-create (default in HSC OLS mode) require activation-request-fwd/bwd set to activate. target-output-power-src and target-output-power-dst range -18.00..15.00 dBm, defaulting to 0 dBm in most cases and -5 dBm for Add/Drop OXcons between a Tributary NMC and an RD20TM/RD09SM NMC.

profile-control applies only to RD20TM operating in card-mode = slte or slte-backhaul, and it runs in Operational Mode only. Syntax: profile-control [type=]<value> [entity=]<value> [direction=]<value> [[profile-data=]<value>]. type is write-attenuation-profile, read-attenuation-profile, create-power-profile, read-power-profile or read-ocm-power; entity is the instance the profile applies to (for example oms-1-8-dwdm-line or nmc-RD20-1-1); direction is tx or rx, but for power-profile only tx is supported. Note that for RD20TM in card-mode = slte the power profile and OCM power are defined at the output of the booster, before the EVOA, not at the DWDM line out port. OMS attenuation values run 0 to 25.50 with N = 776 slices for standardC-band at 6.25 GHz; NMC attenuation values run -10 to 25.50 with N not exceeding 32.

Not much: set pump-<name> only accepts label, admin-state and alarm-report-control. label is a String of length 0..256, admin-state takes lock, unlock or maintenance, and alarm-report-control is allowed or inhibited with default Allowed. Everything else on the pump facility is read-only through show pump-<name>: supporting-card, supporting-port, supporting-facilities, supported-facilities, AID, oper-state (enabled/disabled), avail-state (in-service, out-of-service, normal, abnormal, low-power), managed-by (system or user, only user-created facilities can be user deleted) and pump-type. To change the actual Raman pump power use the separate pump-power command and its target-pump-power attribute. Access mode is Operational and Candidate Configuration mode.

Use set pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> target-pump-power <value>, where pump-id is the integer identifying the pump. target-pump-power is the Raman pump power in dBm, applicable when control-mode is manual, values -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable (default not-applicable), with 0 used for the not-applicable case; on an RPBM card the target-pump-power must be in the range 12 to 30 dBm. If the value is outside the operating range of the Raman sled, the alarm PUMP-Fail (STAT FAIL PSTAT) is raised. The permitted ceiling and floor are readable: show pump-power-<name>/<pump-id> min-target-pump-power max-target-pump-power, both decimal64 with 2 fraction digits over -99.00..99.00 dBm or not-applicable. configured-pump-power shows the power configured in hardware (derived automatically when control-mode is auto, otherwise from target-pump-power) and actual-pump-power shows what is currently measured, default -99.

Read calibration-state on the raman-calibration facility: show raman-calibration-<name> calibration-state. It displays the state of the automatic Raman gain calibration process, with values not-available (calibration has not been triggered or no prior calibration has occurred), in-progress (currently running), up-to-date (completed successfully and current), out-dated (stale due to OTS OLOS, a change in delta pointloss, etc.) and fail (ended with a failure); default is not-available. last-calibration-timestamp gives when the last calibration rpc completed, with or without errors (date-and-time, or never). When the state is fail or out-dated, additional-info (string up to 1024 characters) carries troubleshooting information. Also available: gain-calibration-error (residual gain error in dB after each iteration), calibrated-delta-pointloss (suggested delta-pointloss, -3..3.5 dB) and intermediate-results. Example: show raman-calibration-1-8.

rsc is the Raman card Pilot Tone facility. Syntax: set rsc-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] and show rsc-<name> [supporting-card] [supporting-port] [supporting-facilities] [supported-facilities] [AID] [label] [admin-state] [oper-state] [avail-state] [managed-by] [alarm-report-control] [rsc-power-rx] [rsc-power-tx]. What it reports is the pilot tone power: rsc-power-rx is the received Pilot Tone integrated power and rsc-power-tx is the transmitted Pilot Tone integrated power, both show-only. admin-state takes Unlock, Locked, Maintenance or Unknown, default Unlocked; alarm-report-control is Allowed or Inhibited, default Allowed; oper-state is enabled or disabled with default enabled; managed-by defaults to system. Access: Operational mode and Candidate Configuration mode.

Because the server-layer OMS is not in a monitoring mode that creates it. The spectrum facility is only instantiated by the system when the underlying server layer OMS monitoring-mode is configured either as non-intrusive or ila-with-equalization; the spectrum object is only of relevance if the DGE2 is intended to be used in the NE, and the existence of the managed object depends on the OMS monitoring-mode. Set the OMS monitoring-mode accordingly and the spectrum object appears. Related read-only attribute dge-in-use reports true if the corresponding OMS monitoring-mode is ila-with-equalization, default false. On spectrum you can then set label, admin-state, alarm-report-control and attenuation-setting, a single attenuation value for the entire spectrum, range 0..30 dB, default 0 dB, editable only when attenuation-control-mode = manual and control-mode = auto-max-pw.

Use the spectrum-control object, keyed by name, direction and slice center frequency: add or set spectrum-control-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [attenuation-target <value>] [target-output-power <value>]. direction is ingress or egress, but currently only egress is supported and egress is the default; center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. attenuation-target is the required attenuation for that spectra, range [0..30] dB, default 0, and is only possible to configure when a Dynamic Gain Equalizer, or equivalent, is in use (dge-in-use = 'true'). target-output-power is the intended target output power for the spectra, not-specified or [-55..55] dBm, default not-specified. show adds width (detected width in MHz, 0 if the frequency does not match or no ILAx card or DGE is fiber-connected) and attenuation-actual. Example: set spectrum-control-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/194943750 attenuation-target 1.

Use show spectrum-monitoring-<name>/<direction>/<center-frequency> [width] [lower-frequency] [upper-frequency] [target-actual-power] [power-actual] [psd-actual]. Available in Operational and Candidate Configuration mode; it is show-only. name is a String (length 0..64); direction is ingress or egress, default egress, and only egress is currently supported; center-frequency is the band slice center frequency in MHz and is managed by the system. width is the received NMC width in MHz, default 50000. lower-frequency and upper-frequency give the Media Channel edges in MHz. target-actual-power is the target power calculated by ATPS, relevant when target-power-setting = auto, default -99dBm. power-actual is the currently received power in dBm, default -99; -99dBm means either the power has not yet been measured (the measurement is done by the OCM on the DGE2 card) or no power was detected / there is no appropriate fiber-connection. In the egress direction the power actual is calibrated at the DWDM Line port output, the same reference point where target power is defined. psd-actual is the calculated Power Spectral Density in nW/GHz with 2 digit precision, default not-applicable, and does not depend on the spectra width. Example: show spectrum-monitoring-1-7-dwdm-line2/egress/191968750

Read the contention-check-status attribute of the super-channel. It reports the Contention Check state, which is set via DNA in openwave mode. Values are pending, success, overridden and failk, with default pending. It is only applicable if openwave-contention-check is enabled at the super-channel-group level; openwave-contention-check takes false or true and defaults to false, so with the default you get no contention result. contention-check-status can be supplied on creation: add super-channel-<name> carriers <value> carrier-mode <value> [label <value>] [admin-state <value>] [alarm-report-control <value>] [contention-check-status <value>], and read back with show super-channel-<name> [contention-check-status] alongside carriers, carrier-mode, actual-carrier-mode, capacity, spectral-bandwidth and the state attributes. The related line-system-mode attribute indicates the L1 to L0 power control mode and is openwave. Both commands run in Operational or Candidate configuration mode.

-m is the merge flag: Merge configuration, meaning the command will not fail if the entity already exists. The add command for super-channel-group works in merge mode only, so the -m flag performs a best effort add: if the target entity does not exist it is created, and if it already exists it is updated with any attributes present on the add command. The full form is add -m super-channel-group-<name> [label <value>] [admin-state <lock|unlock|maintenance>] [auto-in-service-enabled <value>] [valid-signal-time <value>] [alarm-report-control <allowed|inhibited>] [line-system-mode <value>] [openwave-contention-check <value>]. Defaults for those attributes are admin-state unlock, alarm-report-control allowed, auto-in-service-enabled false, valid-signal-time 480 minutes (range 1..7200), line-system-mode openwave. The command runs in Operational or Candidate Configuration mode. The same -m merge flag is used by comm-channel, whose add is likewise merge-only.

Use show supported-carrier-mode-<name>/<carrier-mode> [capacity] [client-mode] [baud-rate] [application] [compatibility-id] [status] [supported-subtypes], available in Operational and Candidate configuration mode. carrier-mode is an acronymized code (handle) indicating the optical carrier line mode 4-tuple, formatted <Capacity><ClientMode>.<Baud Rate><Application ID>, a string of length 1..15; examples given are 600E.84P, 100X.73U and 325M.66P. capacity is the net capacity of the optical carrier expressed in gbps. client-mode is the digital client mode of the signal mapped into and transported by the carriers within the superchannel, either ethernet or ethernet-otn. baud-rate is the modulated symbol rate (string). application is the optical transport application ID the mode is optimized for, string length 1..15. compatibility-id identifies the compatible carrier modes that can be applied simultaneously. status is the state of the carrier mode. supported-subtypes lists the subtypes each carrier mode supports, string length 0..32, maximum 20 elements.

Use show supported-gain-range-<name>/<gain-range-type> [gain-range-min] [gain-range-max], available in Operational and Candidate configuration mode; it is a show-only capability command. gain-range-type selects which range you want and takes low, high or standard. gain-range-min is the minimum settable gain-target for that type of range (standard, low or high) and gain-range-max is the maximum settable gain-target for that same range; both are of type gain-value and have no default, since they are reported by the system per card. The name key is documented as a flag to enable or disable access control with values true or false and default false. So to see the concrete gain limits behind a low, standard or high gain range setting, show the supported-gain-range instance for the entity and read gain-range-min and gain-range-max for that gain-range-type.

Different power profiles are supported to reflect different scenarios when using a card. The user is able to define, per card instance, which profile is in effect, and that choice has an impact on the power estimation for the system. To see what a card type offers, use show supported-power-profile-<card-type>/<name> [profile-description] [power-draw] [default], available in Operational and Candidate Configuration Mode. card-type is the card type (string) and name is the profile name (string). profile-description is a description of the profile, string length 0..255. power-draw is the power draw of the associated equipment when not in low-power, expressed as decimal64. default is true or false and tells you whether that profile is the default one for the card type. None of these attributes carry a documented default value; they are read from the card capability data.

The router ID is controlled by router-id-mode on the bgp-instance. router-id-mode is a flag indicating that the router-id is the loopback IP; it takes use-loopback or manual and defaults to use-loopback, so by default the instance takes the loopback IP address. To set it explicitly, choose manual and supply router-id, which specifies the router ID as an IPv6 or IPv4 address; 0.0.0.0/0 is not supported for IPv4 and 0::0.0 is not supported for IPv6. Syntax: add bgp-instance-<instance-id> local-as <value> [description <value>] [router-id-mode <value>] [router-id <value>], and it can be changed later with set bgp-instance-<instance-id> [router-id-mode <value>] [router-id <value>]. instance-id is a string of length 1..255 and local-as is a number in the range 1..4294967295. Example: add bgp-instance-10 local-as 24 router-id-mode use-loopback. Runs in Operational or Candidate Configuration Mode.

On bgp-neighbor the timer defaults are: connect-retry-interval 120 seconds (range 1..65535), the interval between attempts to establish a session with the peer; hold-time 90 seconds (range 3..65535), the time a BGP session is considered active without keepalives or other messages, typically set to 3x the keepalive-interval; and keepalive-interval 30 seconds (range 1..21845), typically 1/3 of the hold-time. negotiated-hold-time is read-only, range 0..65535 seconds, default 0. Yes, you can authenticate the session: secure-session sets the authentication method and takes none or TCP-MD5, default none, and password carries the TCP-MD5 authentication key in ASCII format, a string of 0..80 characters. All of these are settable on add bgp-neighbor-<instance-id>/<remote-address> peer-as <value> ... or later with set. Related read-only state is session-state (Idle, Connect, Active, OpenSent, OpenConfirm, Established, Close, default Idle) and known-errors.

The routes to be advertised to an external AS must exist in the forwarding table installed by an Interior Gateway Protocol (IGP) such as OSPF, or by static routes, but not by BGP itself.
